headline: High-risk write-capable agent paired with a non-runnable course artifact creates medium prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance exposure; no direct evidence of a safe bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and shell, so it may ingest external content as instructions; agent_b is a docs/course artifact with no runtime protections or isolation described. The pairwise bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes above low, but there is no evidence of a shared channel by default.
conditions: IF agent_a reads agent_b content from a shared workspace, clipboard, or MCP feed as instructions, injection becomes active.
IF the orchestrator routes agent_b text into agent_a tool prompts without provenance checks, prompt hijack is possible.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from shared files.
Add provenance tags to all agent_b-derived text.
Require a human review step before agent_a executes instructions from agent_b outputs.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures, while agent_b is a docs-only course artifact with no data classes listed. A shared workspace or copied outputs could leak sensitive material from agent_a into agent_b-facing artifacts; the reverse path is less concerning, but the pair still has a plausible default leakage route if co-located.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or notebook workspace, files can be copied between them.
IF agent_a writes prompts or signatures into artifacts that agent_b publishes or stores, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Separate storage locations for each agent.
Redact secrets before any handoff.
Restrict agent_a outputs to non-sensitive summaries.
Audit shared directories for copied prompts or keys.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has shell, package install, git modification, subprocess, and allowlisted egress; agent_b is not runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities. That makes direct capability conflict limited, with the main risk being agent_a colliding with itself or with external orchestration rather than with agent_b.
conditions: IF agent_b is wrapped in a separate mutable workspace despite being non-runnable, agent_a could still overwrite shared files.
IF the orchestrator gives both agents the same git checkout, agent_a can create conflicts.
mitigations: Use read-only mounts for agent_b assets.
Keep separate git worktrees.
Serialize any writes from agent_a.
Avoid exposing shared mutable directories.
requires-engineering: add lock coordination for shared repositories.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate analysis and modify repositories, while agent_b is a data-engineering course artifact that may consume or present those outputs without verification if wired into a workflow. Because no verification or downstream guardrails are documented, the pair can propagate incorrect agent_a outputs into later work products.
conditions: IF agent_b is used to present or operationalize agent_a outputs without a validation step, errors cascade.
IF agent_a's generated facts are copied into course materials or scripts, downstream mistakes persist.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse of agent_a outputs.
Require citations for any factual claims.
Limit agent_a to draft-only outputs.
Mark agent_b artifacts as non-authoritative.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before publication.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles code, repository metadata, task prompts, and signatures, while agent_b is a public course artifact with no residency or retention controls documented. The mismatch is not a proven breach, but the absence of compliance metadata on agent_b and the presence of sensitive classes on agent_a create a plausible policy gap if data is shared across them.
conditions: IF agent_a data is copied into agent_b-hosted docs, retention and access policies may diverge.
IF any regulated or secret material is routed through the course artifact, compliance controls are unclear.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of agent_b materials.
Publish only sanitized excerpts.
Document retention for any shared artifacts.
Review whether signatures or prompts are regulated in your environment.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
